newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of E.Asia profit growth seen solid.
newsitem.headline: Bank of E.Asia profit growth seen solid.

text.p: Bank of East Asia Ltd is due to kick off the reporting period for Hong Kong's blue-chip banks with solid net profit growth due to a property boom in the territory and expansion in China, analysts said on Friday.
"We had a property boom (in Hong Kong) last year and that of course should benefit the banking sector," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
He expected 1996 net profit of HK$1.85 billion, up 12.8 percent compared with HK$1.64 billion in 1995.
Bank of East Asia posted interim net profit for the six months ended June 30, 1996, of HK$846.92 million compared with HK$687.01 million. It is due to report final results on Monday.
"Mortgage lending has been very strong," said Alex Wong, banking analyst at Dharmala Securities.
"About 43 percent of their loan portfolio is from residential mortgages, which is higher than the market average of 35 to 40 percent and slightly exceeds the recommended ceiling," he said.
Wong forecast 1996 net profit of HK$1.95 billion.
"They are quite aggressive in mortgage lending and have had lots of promotion programmes," said another analqst at a local brokerage who forecast 1996 net profit of HK$1.80 billion.
"Mortgage loan growth is basically the driver."
But Shannon Garrett, banking analyst at SocGen-Crosby Securities, said she expected Bank of East Asia to have lost market share in the mortgage business.
"I am somewhat disappointed in the domestic business at Bank of East Asia, particularly on the mortgage front," she said.
Garrett forecast net profit of HK$1.83 billion and expected the main areas of growth for the bank to be in China. "We are seeing growth in China which is a higher margin business," she said.
Analysts said China operations should contribute about 14-15 percent of net profit in 1996, up from 10 percent in 1995.

"In the last three years the bank has been very actively expanding its presence in China, where it has six branches, five representative offices and joint-venture finance companies," said Asia Equity.
In a banking sector report released this month, it said that "branch presence in China should result in 1996 volume growth above industry norms". It saw net profit of HK$1.79 billion.
Analysts said they also expected improvements in the net interest margin.

"The interest spread has been widening because interest rates have remained steady and banks are able to improve their interest margin," said Wong. "People are shifting their funds from the higher interest account deposits to demand deposits and saving deposits."
However, trade finance was expected to be sluggish.
"It was a very difficult year for trade finance, not only in terms of loan growth but also in terms of the trade related exposure," said Garrett.
Bank of East Asia said charges for bad and doubtful debts, mostly linked to trade finance clients, rose 122 percent in the first half of 1996.
"Overall for the year I am looking for a sharp increase in provisioning but cerainty not of the order that we have had in the past," said Garrett.
After a HK$28.27 million exceptional gain from property sales in the first half of 1996, analysts said they did not expect any property contributions for the second half.
"They still have three (property) projects but both projects will contribute to earnings from 1998 only," said Wong.
Bank of East Asia shares fell HK$0.60 to close Friday morning's session at HK$35.20.
